blocks.etymology: From halcyon, from Latin Alcyone, from Ancient Greek Ἀλκυόνη (Alkuónē), daughter of Aeolus and wife of Ceyx. When her husband died in a shipwreck, Alcyone threw herself into the sea whereupon the gods transformed them both into halcyon birds (kingfishers). When Alcyone made her nest on the beach, waves threatened to destroy it. Aeolus restrained his winds and kept them calm during seven days in each year, so she could lay her eggs. These became known as the "halcyon days," when storms do not occur. Today, the term is used to denote a past period that is being remembered for being happy or successful.

examples.vi: Cô ấy mất hai mươi phút cố chải mái tóc rối của mình.

senses.definition: very complicated and hard to understand or solve

examples.en: The police uncovered a tangled web of lies.
examples.vi: Cảnh sát đã phát hiện một mạng lưới dối trá đầy phức tạp.

thesaurus.definition: highly complex or intricate and occasionally devious

examples: tangled knot
wiktionary.gloss: Mixed up, interlaced.
Intricate.

idioms.gloss: When one tells a simple lie, it may become necessary to tell more complex lies, eventually spiraling out of control and leading to the exposure of the deceit.
idioms.phrase: what a tangled web we weave when first we practice to deceive

known: what a tangled web we weave when first we practice to deceive

wiktionary.gloss: Having thirteen sides and angles, similar to a tridecagon.

blocks.etymology: tri- (“three”) + Latin foliātus (“leaved”) Doublet of tréflé.

thesaurus.definition: (of a leaf shape) having three leaflets

vi_block: Có lá kép ba lá chét (cây).

wiktionary.gloss: Having or comprising three leaves, or (loosely) trifoliolate (with three leaflets) or having leaves with three parts, as the clover plant.
Comprising, abounding with, or featuring trefoils.

blocks.etymology: tri- (“three”) + Latin foliātus (“leaved”) Doublet of tréflé.

wiktionary.gloss: A trifoliate plant

thesaurus.definition: in an imperceptible manner or to an imperceptible degree

wiktionary.gloss: In an unnoticeable manner.
Of or pertaining to a vestibule in a building (or railway coach).
Of, pertaining to, or functioning as a vestibule (body cavity).

examples: vestibular impulse
wiktionary.gloss: Of or pertaining to the vestibule of the inner ear and the perception of body position, balance and movement.
Of or pertaining to the surface of a tooth that is directed outward toward the vestibule of the mouth, including the buccal and labial surfaces, and opposite the lingual (or oral) surface.
A competitive examination used by Brazilian universities to select students.

tatoeba.en: I have a sensitive vestibular system, so that might be part of why car rides make me dizzy and nauseous.
tatoeba.vi: Tôi có hệ tiền đình nhạy cảm, chắc đó là lí do đi xe ô tô khiến tôi chóng mặt và buồn nôn.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English waden, from Old English wadan, from Proto-West Germanic *wadan, from Proto-Germanic *wadaną (“to go, pass through”), from Proto-Indo-European *weh₂dʰ- (“to go”). Cognates include Saterland Frisian waadje (“to wade”), West Frisian wâdzje (“to wade”), Dutch waden (“to wade”), German Low German waden (“to wade”), German waten (“to wade”), Danish vade (“to wade”), Swedish vada (“to wade”), Icelandic vaða (“to wade”), and Latin vādō (“go, walk; rush”).

senses.definition: to walk through water or mud that makes it hard to move forward

examples.en: We had to wade across the shallow river to get home.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi phải lội qua con sông nông để về nhà.

senses.definition: to spend a lot of time reading or dealing with something long or boring

examples.en: I had to wade through dozens of dry reports today.
examples.vi: Hôm nay tôi đã phải đánh vật với hàng chục bản báo cáo khô khan.

senses.vi: làm một cách vất vả; đánh vật với

senses.definition: to join a fight, argument, or debate quickly without thinking carefully

examples.en: The police waded into the angry crowd to stop the riot.
examples.vi: Cảnh sát đã lao vào đám đông giận dữ để dẹp loạn.

thesaurus.definition: walk (through relatively shallow water)

vi_block: Làm (việc gì) một cách khó nhọc, làm một cách vất vả.

wiktionary.gloss: To walk through water or something that impedes progress.

examples: to wade through a dull book
wiktionary.gloss: To progress with difficulty.

examples: wading swamps and rivers
wiktionary.gloss: To walk through (water or similar impediment); to pass through by wading.
To gleam intermittently through clouds or mist.

examples: to wade into a fight or a debate
wiktionary.gloss: To enter recklessly.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English waden, from Old English wadan, from Proto-West Germanic *wadan, from Proto-Germanic *wadaną (“to go, pass through”), from Proto-Indo-European *weh₂dʰ- (“to go”). Cognates include Saterland Frisian waadje (“to wade”), West Frisian wâdzje (“to wade”), Dutch waden (“to wade”), German Low German waden (“to wade”), German waten (“to wade”), Danish vade (“to wade”), Swedish vada (“to wade”), Icelandic vaða (“to wade”), and Latin vādō (“go, walk; rush”).

senses.definition: an act of walking through water or deep mud

examples.en: It was a cold and tiring wade across the stream.
examples.vi: Đó là một chuyến lội qua dòng suối lạnh lẽo và mệt mỏi.

examples: We had to be careful during our dangerous wade across the river.
wiktionary.gloss: An act of wading.
A ford; a place to cross a river.

phrasal_verbs.gloss: To search or progress through with difficulty, as when performing a boring, repetitive research task.
To interrupt someone, or a situation, by doing or saying something abruptly, or forcefully, and usually without thinking about the consequences.
